figures.caption: 圖：午休時間的走廊與樓梯間
figures.description: 午休鐘響後，教室裡已經坐滿趴睡的同學。幾名學生抱著外套坐在樓梯間的台階上，靠著牆閉眼休息；一名男生把頭埋在膝蓋之間。走廊的一張窄木長椅上，兩名學生肩並肩趴著睡，其中一人的手臂垂到地上。樓梯轉角的窗戶透進刺眼的陽光。一位老師正從樓上走下來，坐在台階上的學生只好縮起腳讓路。

questions.stem: 提示：高中生每天在學校的時間很長，但許多學校除了教室以外，很少有讓學生放鬆、休息的地方。請根據下圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖中學生午休時的情形；第二段說明如果由你來規劃一個學生休息空間，你會怎麼設計，並說明這樣設計的理由。

1.explanation_zh: 第一段描述圖中學生午休的情形；第二段要寫「設計」和「理由」兩件事。設計要具體（在哪裡、有什麼設備、怎麼使用），理由要說明這樣設計解決了什麼問題，可以直接連到圖中的陽光、擁擠或姿勢不舒服，也可以用自己午休的經驗。
evidence: 第一段描述圖中學生午休時的情形
並說明這樣設計的理由
1.strategy_zh: 第二段先用假設語氣交代「如果由我設計」，之後每提一項設計就緊接一個理由（說明原因或目的），避免設計和理由分成兩堆。
hints: 第一段：依教室、樓梯、走廊的順序描述，加上陽光與老師經過
第二段：先說地點，再寫兩三項設備或規則
每項設計後面接理由，最後一句說明休息空間的意義

moves.zh: 描述圖中學生午休時的情形
如果由你來規劃一個學生休息空間，你會怎麼設計

content.focus_zh: 第一段要寫出學生在哪裡、用什麼姿勢休息，以及陽光、老師經過等不舒服的細節；第二段要提出具體的設計（地點、設備、分區或使用規則），並為每項設計說明理由，最好連結到圖中的問題或自己的經驗。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段由教室寫到樓梯與走廊；第二段先總述設計，再逐項說明，理由放在設計之後，結尾回扣「學校為什麼需要休息空間」。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在進行式；想像的設計用 would、could（If I could …, I would …），時態要前後一致；so that 表目的。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 空間與設備的字（sofa、cushion、curtain、lighting、bench、hallway、stairs）要用得準確，避免整段只用 comfortable 與 relax。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

outline.topic_sentence_zh: 提出你心中的學生休息空間。

分區或使用規則（睡覺區、閱讀區、預約制度）

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The picture shows what happens at lunch break in many high schools. Since the classrooms are already full of sleeping students, some students have to find other places to rest. Several of them are sitting on the stairs with their jackets in their arms, and one boy is resting his head on his knees. In the hallway, two students are sleeping side by side on a wooden bench. One of them looks very uncomfortable because his arm is hanging down to the floor. Meanwhile, a teacher is walking down the stairs, so the students have to pull in their legs to let him pass.
If I could design a rest area for students, I would turn an empty classroom into a quiet lounge. First, it would have soft sofas and large cushions so that students could lie down comfortably. Second, the windows would have thick curtains to block the strong sunlight. In addition, there would be a small corner with books and board games for students who do not want to sleep. I have these ideas because of my own experience. For example, last semester I often slept on the stairs at noon and woke up with a sore neck, so I could hardly focus in afternoon classes. With a proper rest area, however, students would feel refreshed after lunch. In conclusion, a comfortable place to rest is not a luxury but a basic need for busy students.

paragraphs.function_zh: 描述圖片：教室坐滿後，學生在樓梯與走廊長椅上休息的樣子

paragraphs.function_zh: 理想設計＋理由：把空教室改成休息室，列出三項設計，並用自己在樓梯午睡的經驗說明理由
paragraphs.topic_sentence: If I could design a rest area for students, I would turn an empty classroom into a quiet lounge.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
When the lunch break bell rings, the classrooms in the picture fill up within minutes, and students who cannot find a desk are left to rest wherever they can. Inside the classrooms, every desk is occupied by a classmate sleeping face down. Several of the unlucky ones sit on the cramped steps of the staircase, hugging their jackets like pillows, and one boy has buried his head between his knees. Two others are dozing on a narrow wooden bench in the hallway, shoulder to shoulder, one with his arm hanging awkwardly toward the floor. Harsh sunlight pours through the window at the corner of the stairs, making real sleep almost impossible. Just then, a teacher comes down the steps, and the sleepy students have to pull in their legs to make way for him. In this scene, rest looks more like a struggle than a break.
If I were given the chance to design a rest area, I would transform an unused classroom into what I call a “recharge room.” The room would be divided into two zones. The larger zone, for napping, would have reclining chairs, thick curtains, and soft lighting, because the glare from the windows, as the picture shows, is one of the main reasons students cannot fall asleep. In addition, the smaller zone, separated by bookshelves, would welcome those who prefer to stay awake, offering beanbags, magazines, and a few board games. I would also introduce a simple booking system so that each class could reserve the room on different days, preventing it from becoming as crowded as the hallway. These ideas come from my own experience. For instance, last year I took my naps on the staircase almost every day, and by the seventh period my neck was stiff and my notes were full of half-finished sentences. A short, proper nap, by contrast, can reduce fatigue and make the afternoon far more productive, so a rest space is not a luxury but an investment in learning. Admittedly, the school may worry about cost and supervision, yet most of the furniture could be donated by parents, and student volunteers could take turns keeping the room tidy. In short, a place to rest would show students that the school cares about how well they learn, not just how long they stay in class.

paragraphs.topic_sentence: When the lunch break bell rings, the classrooms in the picture fill up within minutes, and students who cannot find a desk are left to rest wherever they can.

paragraphs.function_zh: 理想設計＋理由：「充電室」分成午睡區與清醒區、加上預約制度，每項設計都對應圖中的問題或自己的經驗，讓步後以見解作結

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 描述細膩並點出休息的困難，設計具體（分區、設備、預約制度）且每項都有對應的理由，經驗與讓步讓論點更完整（內容 5）；設計逐項推進、理由緊接其後，結尾有見解（組織 5）；假設語氣、分詞構句、what 子句正確多樣（文法句構 5）；用字精確（glare、supervision、reclining），但仍以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段依序寫出教室坐滿、樓梯間抱外套、男生靠膝蓋、長椅上手臂垂地與老師經過，但漏了刺眼的陽光（第二段才提到要擋陽光）；第二段的沙發靠墊、厚窗簾、閱讀桌遊角都附理由，並用自己睡樓梯脖子痠的經驗收尾。全文無語言錯誤，句型以 If…would、so that、since 子句為主，變化中等；字彙準確但偏基本，轉承語 First／Second／In addition 稍公式化。

top.comment_zh: 第一段細節完整（教室、樓梯、長椅、陽光、老師讓路），收在 a struggle than a break；第二段分區設計、預約制度、親身經驗、讓步（經費與管理）再回扣主旨，層次清楚。分詞構句、插入語、not…but… 等句型多樣，字彙（glare、reclining chairs、fatigue、supervision）精準。小瑕疵：preventing it from becoming as crowded as the hallway 與圖不太吻合（圖中最擠的是教室與樓梯，走廊長椅只有兩人），可改成 the classrooms 或 the staircase。

steady.comment_zh: 兩段分工清楚：第一段寫出學生在樓梯、長椅的姿勢與老師經過，第二段提出教室改成休息室的設計，每項設計都有 so that／to block 的理由，再以親身經驗與結論收尾。第一段沒寫到刺眼陽光，細節略少；用字準確但偏平實，句型以簡單句與 so／because 為主，沒有文法或拼字錯誤。

top.comment_zh: 第一段細節完整（趴睡的教室、抱外套的學生、窄長椅、刺眼陽光、老師經過），並以 struggle 收束；第二段依序提出分區設計、理由、親身經驗、讓步（成本與管理）與結論，理由都連回圖中的問題。句型多樣、時態一致（If I were …, I would …），用字精準（cramped、glare、reclining chairs、beanbags），沒有任何錯誤。僅 the classrooms 用複數，圖中只有一間教室，影響極小。
